correctness.rationale: Independently embedded both grids in the common mesh of width h/2. For a coarse-cell phase z and b=1+z, their paired fine-node interpolation vectors are (1,b/2) and (conj(b)/2,1). The fine mass block h/12 times [[4,conj(b)],[b,4]] gives auto-Gram h(4+2|b|²)/12 and cross-Gram h conj(b)(5+|b|²/4)/12, hence exactly the stated squared principal cosines for all N≥3. Writing x=|cos(ω/2)| gives 1−γ=(1−x)²(2−x)/(2(1+2x²)), γ increasing in x. This confirms the Nyquist zero, constant eigenspace, sharp first-mode gap and coefficient 1/192 in the angular fourth-order expansion of 1−γ². For centered k, the same identity gives 1−μ≥2|k|⁴/(3N⁴), yielding a uniform summable tail when the rescaled time is bounded below. Fixed normalized interpolants and hence their rank-one projectors converge to the Fourier projectors (in trace norm for each projector). The finite-mode/tail decomposition proves the critical and supercritical trace-norm limits; the vanishing-time strong limit follows by fixed-mode convergence and density. No uploaded script was run.
residual_risks: For very small τ and the finitely many N with floor(τN⁴)=0, the zeroth power is the identity, not finite rank. The trace-norm assertion refers to the eventual sequence of positive powers, so this wording does not affect the limit.
At τ=0 the infinite-dimensional identity is not trace class; only strong convergence is established there.

checked_sources: Frozen RESULT.md, exact gap and three-regime operator convergence
value.rationale: Uniform piecewise-linear finite elements and a midpoint shift are natural projector discretizations. The exact coefficient, time scale and trace-class mode control show an emergent fourth-order rather than second-order smoothing law from two nearby ranges. The norm gap is useful for estimating alternating-projection convergence, while trace-norm convergence and the heat trace determine collective behavior not captured by the gap alone.
residual_risks: No generalization to other offsets, degrees or nonuniform grids, or positivity of a fourth-order heat kernel, is asserted.
